beats.care: If you rely on public toilets during commutes, small costs may add up. It is only a proposal for now.
beats.what: BMC's draft Pay-and-Use Policy 2026 raises fees: women's urinals Rs 2 to Rs 5, bathing Rs 5 to Rs 10, men's urinals Rs 1.
beats.why: BMC wants a revenue model to pay for upkeep, including ads on up to 40% of toilet space.

cards.body: Up from Rs 2. Men, who pay nothing now, may pay Rs 1.
cards.caption: Proposed women's urinal fee

cards.body: The plan also adds QR codes and an app for complaints, and lets sites host EV charging, ATMs and tea stalls.
Women already pay at urinals while men don't. The proposal makes both pay, but women still pay more.

cards.q: Fair to charge for public urinals?

opts: It's a proposal awaiting a BMC meeting
cards.q: What is the status of BMC's toilet fee hike?
cards.why: The draft goes to a Group Leaders' meeting at BMC HQ; no start date is set.

hook: Will using a public toilet in Mumbai *cost more* soon?

learn.t: Mumbai has over 3,000 BMC public toilets across 26 wards, plus 846 roadside ones run by private agencies.

sources.name: Free Press Journal
sources.title: BMC Proposes Hike In Public Toilet Charges Under Pay-And-Use Policy 2026; Women's Urinal Fee May Rise To ₹5, Men To Pay ₹1

tldr: BMC has proposed raising public toilet charges, including Rs 5 for women's urinals and a new Rs 1 fee for men.
